subject: Physical Education
name: Basic 2 Physical Education
description: The Basic 2 Physical Education curriculum builds on foundational skills, focusing on locomotor movements, manipulative skills with balls, balancing, rhythmic movements, and understanding physical fitness and social values in sports.

strands.title: MOTOR SKILL AND MOVEMENT PATTERNS
strands.description: Developing competence in motor skills and movement patterns for various physical activities.

subStrands.title: LOCOMOTOR, MANIPULATIVE AND RHYTHMIC SKILLS
subStrands.description: Developing locomotor, manipulative and rhythmic skills.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate competence in the motor skills and movement patterns needed to perform a variety of physical activities (games, athletics gymnastics and dance)

indicators.description: Travel (move) in straight, curved, and zigzag pathways, using the following locomotor movements: walking, running, leaping, jumping, and skipping.

exemplars.description: Identify the pathways such as straight, curved, and zigzag.
Mark these pathways and guide them to move through walking, and running, etc.

indicators.description: Forward and backward skip without a rope.

exemplars.description: From standing position with feet together, jump at spot with double take off and double landing flexed arms rotating at the shoulders clockwise.
Skip on the spot using personal space.

indicators.description: Roll a ball from stationary to a given point and back, using hands.

exemplars.description: Place a ball in front, bend the trunk forward and place the palm behind the ball, roll the ball forward whiles moving from one point to another.
Learners can further use bats or sticks to roll the ball to challenge the fast learners.

indicators.description: Demonstrate balance on the ground and on objects, using bases of support other than both feet.

exemplars.description: Demonstrate balance on the ground by sitting on the ground, raise your feet off the ground and support the trunk with your hands.
Sit on a chair and lift your feet off the ground guide learners to identify the chair as the base of support.

indicators.description: Transfer weight from feet to hands and from hands to feet, landing with control.

exemplars.description: Transfer weight from the feet to the hands sideways by bending the trunk laterally and placing the hand on the ground.
Transfer weight momentarily from feet to one hand to the other in hand stand position.

indicators.description: Strike a ball continuously in an upward or forward motion, using a hand and foot

exemplars.description: Stand at shoulder width apart with the foot opposite the striking hand slightly forward.
Toss a ball up and wing the arm forward to strike the ball at the bottom upward.

indicators.description: Strike a ball continuously in an upward or forward motion, using a short-handled paddle (table tennis bat, tennis racket.

exemplars.description: Learners grip a bat/paddle with both hands.
Learners swing the bat/paddle fast to strike a stationary balloon from down and upward with a follow through.

indicators.description: Perform the overhand throw pattern.

exemplars.description: Extent the arm with the ball above the head as you step forward with the opposite leg.
Swing the extended arm forward to throw the ball over the hand.

indicators.description: Throw a ball to a partner using the underhand, overhand and sidearm throw pattern.

exemplars.description: Use the earlier stance pattern but this time stretch the throwing arm down and flex the trunk sideways toward the throwing arm.
Swing the hand quickly and forcefully to throw the ball forward whiles extending the trunk upward and forward.

indicators.description: Catch a flying ball below the waist.

exemplars.description: Learners stand straight, shoulder width apart, with the foot opposite the throwing hand slightly forward.
As the ball enters their palms, they flex their elbow joints (withdrawing it backwards) whiles catching the ball simultaneously to reduce the impact.

indicators.description: Kick a stationary ball using a smooth continuous running approach.

exemplars.description: Place a ball at stationary position. Move back about 5m away from the ball.
Run and kick the ball forward with the instep of the foot.

indicators.description: Hand-dribble by controlling a ball for a sustained period.

exemplars.description: Learners bounce ball continuously on the spot or while moving for a sustained period.
Organise a mini handball or basketball game.

indicators.description: Demonstrate the different effects of varying arm and hand speeds when hand-dribbling a ball.

exemplars.description: Learners bounce balls (dribble) from one point to the other with varying speed.
Help learners to understand that varying the arms and hands speed enables the player to control his or her movement.

indicators.description: Foot-dribble by controlling a ball on the ground.

exemplars.description: Arrange cones in different patterns and learners to dribble balls through the cones at their own pace.
Organise a mini football game for learners to apply the skill in real life situation.

indicators.description: Clap and dance to beat (rhythm)

exemplars.description: Learners clap a beat and dance to the beat. Emphasis on coordination in clapping to the beat and coordination dancing.

indicators.description: Identify the right and left sides of the body and movement from right to left.

exemplars.description: Learners identify their left side and the right side.
Play music and as they dance signal them by mentioning either left side or right side for them to move toward that direction.

indicators.description: Roll forward (a forward roll) from standing position and back to standing.

exemplars.description: Squat in front of a spread mat/safe floor. Place hands on the mat/floor and tuck the chin to touch the chest.
From this position, push with the hands and roll forward in a round form and back to the standing.

strands.title: MOVEMENT CONCEPTS, PRINCIPLES AND STRATEGIES
strands.description: Understanding movement concepts, principles, and strategies.

subStrands.title: SPACE AWARENESS, DYNAMICS, RELATIONS, BODY MANAGEMENT AND STRATEGIES
subStrands.description: Understanding space, dynamics, and body management.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of movement concepts, principles, and strategies that apply to the learning and performance of physical activities

indicators.description: Explain open spaces

exemplars.description: From their personal space, ask them to move (jog, run at varied speed) to open space within the working boundaries.

indicators.description: Distinguish between 'a hop and a jump'.

exemplars.description: Hopping involves taking off on one foot and land on the same foot. Jumping also involves taking off with both feet and land on both feet.
Galloping involves moving one leg leading and the other is rapidly brought forward to it whiles sliding is one count movement to the side.

indicators.description: Compare the body parts.

exemplars.description: Learners identify that apart from deformity all body parts are almost the same.
Learners compare right hand with the left hand, etc.

indicators.description: Identify types of base of support when practicing movement skills.

exemplars.description: Learners identify types of base of support as the feet, the hands, etc.

indicators.description: Identify the roles of body parts not directly involved in catching objects.

exemplars.description: Learners understand that the body parts that are not involved in catching the ball help to stabilize the body in absorbing the impact of the ball.

indicators.description: Identify opportunities to use underhand and overhand movement (throw) patterns.

exemplars.description: Guide learners to understand that underhand and overhand throw are used in games such as netball, basketball, and handball, etc. for passing and shooting.

subStrands.title: AEROBIC CAPACITY, STRENGTH, ENDURANCE AND FLEXIBILITY

contentStandards.description: Assess and maintain a level of physical fitness to improve health and performance.

indicators.description: Perform four continuous abdominal curls.

exemplars.description: Learners to lie on the back with fit flat, knees bent and arms on the floor by side with palms down.
Lift the head and shoulders forward with hand support and back to the floor on two counts rhythm.

indicators.description: Perform two set of four continuous abdominal curls.

exemplars.description: Lift the head and shoulders forward to about 45 degrees angle with hand support and back to the floor on two counts rhythm.
Learners repeat another set of the number they perform after 6 minutes' rest to test their abdominal muscular endurance.

indicators.description: Perform lower back stretch.

exemplars.description: Learners lie face down with feet together and arm stretched sideways.
Learners lift their head and chest up without using the arms as support up to their limit.

indicators.description: Identify the various components of human body (bones, muscles, etc.)

exemplars.description: Use a wall chart of human skeletal system to discuss various components of human system such as bones, muscles, lungs liver, heart, etc.

strands.title: PHYSICAL FITNESS CONCEPTS, PRINCIPLES AND STRATEGIES
strands.description: Understanding fitness concepts for health and performance.

subStrands.title: FITNESS PROGRAMME, HEALTHY DIET, SAFETY AND INJURIES, SUBSTANCES/DRUGS AND BODY COMPOSITION
subStrands.description: Concepts related to fitness, health, and safety.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of physical fitness concepts, principles, and strategies to improve health and performance.

indicators.description: Explain why people participate in physical activities three to four times each week, for at least 30 minutes.

exemplars.description: Learners' their fitness records on Monday of every week to find out the number of time parents have signed that their ward participated in 30 minutes' physical activities.
Discuss why people participate in physical activities three to four times each week, for at least 30 minutes as to improve their fitness, endurance, cardio-vascular endurance, etc.

indicators.description: Mention the components of physical fitness.

exemplars.description: Learners identify the five major components of physical fitness as cardiovascular, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility, body composition.

indicators.description: Sort food into different groups.

exemplars.description: List some foods items and allow learners to sort them into below groups as home work: Carbohydrate, Fruit, Vegetables, Protein.

indicators.description: Explain why it is safer to stretch a warm muscle rather than a cold muscle.

exemplars.description: Learners explain that warmed muscles are elastic and can stretch with less damage as cool muscles in physical activity.

indicators.description: Classify PE equipment into new and old.

exemplars.description: Place PE equipment like discus, javelin, etc. on a table and guide learners to sort them into new and old by their appearance and usage.

indicators.description: Identify types of drugs commonly used by adolescents.

exemplars.description: Guide them to mention common drugs used in their community and list them.

strands.title: VALUES AND PSYCHO-SOCIAL CONCEPTS, PRINCIPLES AND STRATEGIES
strands.description: Developing values and social skills through physical activity.

subStrands.title: SELF-RESPONSIBILITY, SOCIAL INTERACTION, GROUP DYNAMICS AND CRITICAL THINKING
subStrands.description: Values, social interaction, and critical thinking.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate value and utilize knowledge of psychological and sociological concepts, principles, and strategies that apply to the learning and performance of physical activity.

indicators.description: Accept responsibility for one's own behaviour in a group activity.

exemplars.description: As learners perform physical activity they develop values like honesty, sincerity, integrity, accountability, fairness, tolerance, respect, patriotism, etc.

indicators.description: Participate in a variety of group settings (e.g., partners, small groups, and large groups) without interfering with others.

exemplars.description: Discuss with learners as they perform practical activity values such as teamwork, cooperation, patience, respect, tolerance, etc.

indicators.description: Participate positively in physical activities rely on cooperation.

exemplars.description: Emphasis during physical activity that without cooperation learners cannot positively work together positively in physical activities.

indicators.description: Collect data and record progress toward mastery of a motor skill in physical activity.

exemplars.description: Learners keep records of the progress in physical activity, appreciate their effort and work extra for improvement.
